posts.author: bernardb
posts.content_md:
Hi,

I have a Hughes Ruby Laser (rangefinder?).

I would *really* really like to fire it someday. The thing is, I cannot figure out how to hook up the components. I am not an electronic tech and have very little knowledge of circuits and such. Looking thru Sam's Laser FAQ is of no use to me because I cannot build a circuit from scratch. The guy I bought the laser from said it was "complete". If that is the case, do any of you have a clue as to how I connect the parts together?

Please have a look at is at this address:

[http://gallery.mac.com/bernardmac#100048](http://gallery.mac.com/bernardmac#100048)

I can supply wiring and soldering and an external power supply but I have *zero* knowledge about the rest of what needs to be done to fire this beast...any help available for a layman?

Thanks a lot!

Bernard

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
Ron is the best! He has helped me imeasurably. 

Have you seen these pages?

[http://www.repairfaq.org/sam/laserpic/hbl1pics.htm#hrf](http://www.repairfaq.org/sam/laserpic/hbl1pics.htm#hrf)

[http://www.repairfaq.org/sam/laserssc.htm#sscsg8](http://www.repairfaq.org/sam/laserssc.htm#sscsg8)

This is the trigger:

[http://www.repairfaq.org/sam/laserpic/hugrf-9.jpg](http://www.repairfaq.org/sam/laserpic/hugrf-9.jpg)

The Pulse Forming Network is labled in your picture. It looks like you need a power supply. It also looks like you need to buy a diode, transistor, resistor and capacitor. The transformer should be burried inside one of your parts.

But Ron is the expert. He has made holograms with surplus Ruby lasers.

Thanks again!

Bernard

posts.author: glajciorz
posts.content_md:
> **bernardb:** If I use this laser to make a pulsed hologram, how in the heck do I do the alignment of all the optical elements? Do I try to point an alignment laser (ie Diode Laser) in EXACTLY the same path as the pulse will be following?

Why not ? I used such an approach an it was easy to align everything, but my alignment diode laser got burned (either by backreflected IR, visible light from flashlamp and green light). Looks funny under microscope - most of diode's structure evaporated 

Maybe old HeNe serve better as an aligning laser.

What is the size of your KTP crystal ?

greetings

Adam
